Yes, NovaLearn should fund the advanced OCR work before accelerating Teams integration, based on current support demand, onboarding impact, and official roadmap status.

- **Support demand**: Scanned policy documents are the primary driver of citation errors and onboarding delays, making the Advanced OCR Pipeline the highest technical priority [NL-001-S08]. Support demand is severe: 27% of May support tickets were related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs, and the CTO states the OCR pipeline is a "critical system stability requirement" to unclog the support queue [NL-015-S06].
- **Onboarding impact**: OCR and scanned PDF ingestion remain the primary onboarding bottleneck [NL-016-S01]. Solving the underlying data ingestion and citation problem first is essential, because building Teams now would just deliver inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience [NL-015-S06]. The official roadmap confirms accuracy and grounding (citation extraction/parsing for scanned legacy docs) is a core engineering theme driving onboarding delays [NL-014-S01].
- **Roadmap status**: The official roadmap states Teams is in the design phase for Q4 2026 and is not generally available [NL-001-S08] [NL-032-S05]. The CTO affirms Teams cannot be rushed without a complete redesign of the auth layer, risking a tenant-isolation breach [NL-015-S06]. The official roadmap supersedes the sales overclaim in [NL-023-S04], which inaccurately described Teams as "almost ready"; the internal note clarifies it is in an early proof-of-concept phase lacking security controls. Therefore, acceleration would break security protocols and OCR remains the top priority for August [NL-015-S06].
